conditions: Normalized quantum state with finite position and canonical momentum variances in the same Cartesian direction and sufficient operator-domain regularity for the canonical commutator expectation (or weak-form identity) to hold.

symbols.\\sigma_p: Standard deviation of canonical momentum in the same direction as position

spoken_aliases: sigma sub x times sigma sub p is greater than or equal to h bar divided by two
position standard deviation times the standard deviation of canonical momentum in the same direction is at least half the reduced planck constant

evidence: For a normalized state psi, let X and P denote centered position and momentum operators. Cauchy-Schwarz gives sigma_x sigma_p=||X psi|| ||P psi|| >= |<X psi,P psi>| >= |Im <X psi,P psi>|. The canonical commutator [x,p]=i hbar implies the last magnitude is hbar/2 when the commutator identity is valid (including its weak form). This bounds intrinsic state standard deviations, not instrument errors.
